archetype.name: Play-In Team (glass problem)
archetype.definition: A Phoenix team with a league-average offense and a real rim deterrent whose 3-5 start is an honest reflection of a defense leaking threes and rebounds, and which looks like a play-in fight at best until the glass gets fixed.

report.headline: A fine offense undone by the league's worst defensive glass
report.take:
Phoenix at 3-5 is about what it has played like. The W vs Pt Diff is 0 and the margin implies exactly 3 wins, so there is no close-game luck to hide behind. The Net Rtg of -6.4 ranks 23rd and the site has the Suns 25th of 30. The offense is fine: an ORtg of 113.8 sits right at the league's 113.4, built on shooting (eFG % 54.7, 8th; 3P % 36.1, 10th) rather than free throws, where a FT Rate of 23.6 ranks 26th. The trouble is a DRtg of 120.2, 27th in the league.

That defense has one strong part and one broken part. Teams shoot only 60.8% at the rim against Phoenix, 3rd-best, and the Suns force turnovers at a top-10 clip. But they finish possessions worse than anyone. DRB % is 65.8, dead last and 6.6 points under the league, and RPG of 39.3 is also 30th. Opposing centers are putting up 25 points and 16 rebounds a game. Opponents also hit 38.2% from three against them, 27th. History says the rebounding is the anomaly: last season's DRB % was 71.9 and every season before that was in the mid-70s, with a defense that ranked 10th. A collapse that sharp in eight games is partly sample, but the frontcourt grade of C- suggests some of it is personnel.

The individual numbers are noisy, but they tell a story. Devin Booker carries a 29.4 USG % at a 59.9 TS % and has scored 202 points. Yet the team's net rating with him on the floor is 30 points worse than with him off, and the backcourt grades a D+ because Jalen Green (48 TS %) and Collin Gillespie (41.7 TS %) are shooting poorly in heavy minutes. Miles Bridges is the bright spot, 5th of 85 on the power forward tab with a 3.7 BPM. Luke Kennard (75.1 TS %) and Ryan Dunn (+34.3 On-Off) have been the most productive bench pieces. Eight-game On-Off figures swing wildly, so read them as hints, not verdicts.

The direction is mildly encouraging. October was 1-3 with 124.5 allowed a game, including an 83-124 opener at Portland. November is 2-2 with 112.75 allowed, and the last five games are 4.85 points a game better than the season margin. If the glass returns even to last year's level, this looks more like the roughly .500 team of 2025-26 than the 31-win pace the season rate implies.

strengths.title: Efficient half-court shooting offense
strengths.body: The Suns rank 8th in eFG % and 10th in 3P %, which keeps their ORtg right around league average despite rarely getting to the line. This fits the franchise's recent profile: eFG % has sat between 53.5 and 56.5 every season on the sheet. It should hold, though it lacks a free-throw floor on cold nights.

strengths.title: Rim deterrence and forced turnovers
strengths.body: Opponents shoot 60.8% within four feet, 3rd-best and well under the league's 65.2, and the Suns force turnovers at the 7th-best rate. That is a better rim profile than any recent Phoenix season on the sheet. The catch is that opponents still get to the rim more often than average, and the misses Phoenix forces are being rebounded by the other team.

strengths.title: Bridges and the role players
strengths.body: Miles Bridges ranks 5th of 85 at power forward with a 3.7 BPM, giving the frontcourt a reliable two-way presence. Kennard's 75.1 TS % and Dunn's +34.3 On-Off point to bench lineups that work. The shooting from Kennard will cool, but Dunn's minutes look like they should grow.

concerns.title: Worst defensive rebounding in the league
concerns.body: A DRB % of 65.8 ranks 30th, and opposing centers average 16 rebounds and 25 points. Last season's DRB % was 71.9, so this is new rather than structural, but a C- frontcourt behind Bridges gives little reason to think it snaps back on its own. Until it improves, every forced miss is a coin flip.

concerns.title: Perimeter defense against point guards
concerns.body: Opposing point guards score 35.75 a game, the most in the league, and account for 30.1% of the points against Phoenix versus a league share of 22.4%. Opponents hitting 38.2% from three is partly luck, but the point guard leak is consistent enough over eight games to be a scheme or personnel problem.

concerns.title: Backcourt efficiency beyond Booker
concerns.body: Green's 48 TS % and -5.6 BPM, and Gillespie's 41.7 TS %, explain the D+ backcourt grade. Both play heavy minutes. Shooting that low in a small sample usually rises, but the starters' On-Off numbers are the worst on the team.

trend.note: October was 1-3 with 124.5 allowed a game; November is 2-2 at even scoring, and the last five games run 4.85 points a game better than the season margin.

weekAhead.headline: Four home games, two elite tests, two openings
weekAhead.body:
Four of five games are in Phoenix, and the week splits neatly. San Antonio (8-2, Net Rtg 10.3) and the Lakers (9-2, ORtg 122.5, 1st) are among the league's best and expose exactly what Phoenix does badly. The Spurs pound the glass at 48.5 rebounds a game. The Lakers lead the league in FT Rate and have a point guard attack that will test the Suns' worst defensive spot.

The Clippers (2-7) and Charlotte (3-7) are the chances. The Clippers give up the second-most points to shooting guards, a clear opening for Booker. Charlotte has the league's worst offense but rebounds its own misses at the 3rd-best rate, a genuine danger for the league's worst defensive-rebounding team. The week ends on a back-to-back at Denver, whose defense allows the fewest points to shooting guards. Two or three wins would be a good week.

keyMatchups.title: The glass against San Antonio
keyMatchups.body: The Spurs rank 3rd in RPG and 4th in DRB %, while Phoenix ranks 30th in both. San Antonio also turns it over the least in the league, which blunts the Suns' turnover-forcing. Phoenix needs a hot shooting night to offset the extra possessions.

keyMatchups.title: Booker's matchup swing
keyMatchups.body: The Clippers allow 32.33 points a game to shooting guards, 29th in the league. Denver allows a league-low 16.13. Booker's usage makes these two games the clearest read on how far he can carry the offense.

keyMatchups.title: Charlotte's second chances
keyMatchups.body: Charlotte's ORtg of 101 is last in the league, but its ORB % of 31.8 ranks 3rd. Its defense also allows 40.8% from three, worst in the league. This should be a win built on shooting, but only if Phoenix finishes its defensive possessions.

weekAhead.watch: Whether the November defensive improvement survives the Spurs' and Lakers' size and shotmaking, especially on the defensive glass.

restOfSeason.body:
The record is honest, so there is no luck correction coming in either direction. Improvement has to come from the defense. The rebounding collapse and opponents' 38.2% three-point shooting are the two numbers most likely to move back toward normal. The franchise's recent DRB % sits well above this year's, and opponent three-point shooting tends to drift toward the league average. The rim protection is real and the offense is stable, so the Suns should play closer to average than their 31-win pace suggests.

That still likely leaves them short of last season's 45 wins. Most of the guard rotation is inefficient, the frontcourt grade is weak outside Bridges, and the Pacific already has two strong starts above them. A realistic range lands in the mid-to-high 30s, which puts them in the play-in conversation rather than out of it. Better starter lineups around Booker are the upside path.
swingFactors: Defensive rebounding returning toward last season's level
Whether Booker's lineups stop bleeding points

confidence.note: Eight games; On-Off and opponent shooting are very noisy this early.
